/.title: Free Conference Poster Maker for Researchers | Postr
/.description: Free conference poster maker for researchers. Print-ready sizes, discipline-appropriate palettes, BibTeX citations. No signup, no paywall, no PowerPoint.
copy: Postr is a free poster editor built for researchers. Pick a template, write with guidance, check your figures, share a link for comments, and export. No design skills needed, no paywall.
Smart templates: conference-ready layouts with discipline-specific palettes, and APA, SfN and ECNP size presets built in.
Figure readability: paste your R or Python plotting code and see whether the axis labels will still be readable at print size, with a copy-ready fix.
Writing guide: section-by-section tips, word count targets, and a checklist to follow from intro to conclusion.

/about.title: How Postr Works: Features for Academic Posters
/about.description: See how Postr handles authors and affiliations, BibTeX citations, Greek symbols, print sizing, and figure readability: the parts other poster tools get wrong.
copy: Postr is a free academic poster editor for students and researchers. It exists because the usual tools were built for something else.
Enter institutions once, then click to assign them to authors. Superscript numbering stays in sync when you add or remove an affiliation.
Export a .bib from your reference manager and drop it in. Postr reads BibTeX, RIS and EndNote files and formats the reference list for you.
Every poster starts at a real print size, so what you see on screen is what the print shop produces.

/chart-chooser.title: Chart Chooser: Which Chart Fits Your Data? | Postr
/chart-chooser.description: Paste a table or answer three short questions and get ranked, journal-style chart suggestions with captions. Download SVG or PNG. Free, no signup.
copy: Paste a table, upload a CSV or Excel file, or answer three short questions — the chooser ranks the figures that fit your data, drawn as journal-style panels with captions. Download any panel as SVG or PNG. Free, no account, and your data never leaves the browser.
Every suggestion explains itself in methods voice: what shape your data has, and why that chart form reads more accurately than the alternatives.
No data yet? Walk through the three questions and start from a worked example with believable numbers, then swap in your own.
Need the figure on a conference poster? Postr is a free academic poster editor with the same chart engine built in, plus a print-readability check for figures you already have.
